q: Sound is a form of ____ that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium.
e: Sound is a form of energy that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium. Energy here means the capacity to do work.

q: Sound wave is produced by a ____ placed in a medium.
e: Sound wave is produced by a vibrating object placed in a medium. The physics in this sentence is built around vibrating object.

q: The pressure changes occur ____ in the medium by vibrating object.
e: The pressure changes occur alternately in the medium by vibrating object. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: Sound wave propagates as a series of ____ like longitudinal waves on a vibrating spring.
e: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and rarefaction like longitudinal waves on a vibrating spring. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a ____ to propagate.
e: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate. The physics in this sentence is built around medium.

q: Sound wave cannot travel through ____.
e: Sound wave cannot travel through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: The compression is created in the medium as the vibrating object ____.
e: The compression is created in the medium as the vibrating object pushes molecules together. The physics in this sentence is built around pushes molecules together.

q: The compression region has ____.
e: The compression region has higher pressure. Higher pressure here means force acting normally on unit area. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: When the object moves back, the molecules are spread out and ____ is created and the pressure of that region is low.
e: When the object moves back, the molecules are spread out and rarefaction is created and the pressure of that region is low. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than ____ and lower than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$.
e: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than $20 \text{ Hz}$ and lower than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: This interval of frequency is called the ____ (or) hearing range.
e: This interval of frequency is called the audible range (or) hearing range. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: Sound waves with frequencies greater than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$ are called ____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies greater than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$ are called ultrasounds. Ultrasounds names sound waves with frequencies greater than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$.

q: Some objects vibrating with frequencies under $20 \text{ Hz}$ produces sound which cannot be heard by ____.
e: Some objects vibrating with frequencies under $20 \text{ Hz}$ produces sound which cannot be heard by human. The physics in this sentence is built around human.

q: This is called ____.
e: This is called infrasound. Infrasound names this.

q: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the ____ of the medium.
e: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the density of the medium. Density here means mass per unit volume. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: The denser the medium is, the ____ the speed because the particles of the medium are tightly bound together.
e: The denser the medium is, the greater the speed because the particles of the medium are tightly bound together. The physics in this sentence is built around greater.

q: At $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ the speed of sound in air is ____.
e: At $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ the speed of sound in air is $332 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $332 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

q: Whenever the air temperature increases by $1^{\circ}\text{C}$, speed of sound will increase by ____.
e: Whenever the air temperature increases by $1^{\circ}\text{C}$, speed of sound will increase by $0.2\%$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The speed of sound in air can be expressed as ____.
e: The speed of sound in air can be expressed as $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$.

q: Here $T$ is given in ____ and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: Here $T$ is given in K and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around K.

q: The above relation can be approximated by ____.
e: The above relation can be approximated by $v = 332 + 0.6(T - 273)$. The physics in this sentence is built around $v = 332 + 0.6(T - 273)$.

q: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by ____ with temperature rise by one degree ($1^{\circ}\text{C}$ or $1\text{K}$).
e: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by $0.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with temperature rise by one degree ($1^{\circ}\text{C}$ or $1\text{K}$). Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.
